leadIn: How do you usually learn new English words? Do you remember them a week later?

prediction.question: What do you think is the best way to remember new words?
options: Read the list ten times in one evening
Test yourself again after longer and longer breaks

preTeach.definition: a test you do to find out if an idea is true

ccq.question: Do scientists do experiments to find out new things?

preTeach.definition: to look at or study something again

ccq.question: When you review a list, is it the first time you see it?

gist.question: What is the article mainly about?
options: The life of a German scientist
Why we forget, and how to remember for longer
Why tests are bad for students
gist.explanation: It explains the forgetting curve and ways to fight it.

extraQuestion.question: What does the last paragraph do?
extraQuestion.explanation: It tells you what to do with the new words in this text.

response: This platform uses the ideas in this article. Which idea surprised you most, and will it change how you study?

phrases.meaning: other people have the same experience
study with a lot of effort
be going to do something very soon
check what you know without help

examples: Have you ever studied hard for a test, done well, and then a few weeks later realised that you had forgotten almost everything?
Have you ever forgotten someone's name a minute after you heard it?

discovery.question: Does the question ask about a specific time, or about any time in your life?
discovery.explanation: Have you ever + past participle asks about experiences at any time up to now.

grammar.uzNote: O'zbek tilida bu zamonning aniq o'xshashi yo'q. Present perfect (have/has + V3) o'tmishda bo'lib, hozirgacha davom etayotgan yoki hozirga natijasi bor ish uchun: I have read it (o'qiganman).

examples: Instead of studying something ten times in one evening, it is much more effective to study it a few times with longer and longer breaks in between: after one day, then three days, then a week, then a month.
Learning a word in a story is far easier than learning it from a list.

discovery.question: Why does the writer use “much” before “more effective”?
options: Because effective is a short word
